scope: Proposition 4.7 (Rest preparation) of the manuscript “The spacetime Penrose inequality with charge and original-data rigidity” (preprints/The-spacetime-Penrose-inequality-with-charge-and-original-data-rigidity-October-5-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 84ca5bc05bc907a1), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 20. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let the data satisfy Definition 2.1 and E > |P|. Assume θ+(S) ≤ 0 on every boundary component. More generally, one may prescribe a fixed sign σ ∈ {−1, 1} on each component and assume H + σ trS K ≤ 0 there. Set m = p E2 − |P|2. There are smooth data (gj, Kj, Ej, Bj) on the same oriented exterior Ω, with the same closed forms α1, α2, having the following properties. (1) Both charges are exactly QE, QB. Charged DEC is strict everywhere; for some cj > 0 and a fixed 0 < δ0 < 1, inf |Y |gj ≤1 Dgj (Y ) ≥ cjr−3−δ0 y on the far end. Every boundary component has strictly negative future expansion, or strictly negative prescribed expansion H + σ trS K in the fixed-sign variant. (2) In a rest chart y, gj − δ = Oℓ(r−1 y ) and Rgj = Oℓ(r−3−δ0 y ) for every ℓ. The tensor Kj is compactly supported, and the two flux forms have components O1(r−2 y ). The constraint densities are integrable and the metric is complete with S included. (3) The rest ADM momentum is zero and its energy satisfies Ej → m. The fields and tensors converge to the original data smoothly on every compact subset of Ω. (4) There are ϵj ↓ 0 such that gj ≥ (1 − ϵj)g on all of Ω, and Amin,gj (S) −→ Amin,g(S). (4.20) No uniform bound on the compact geometry of this sequence is asserted or needed. Each prepared datum is fixed before the subsequent elliptic comparison parameters are chosen.
